newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G settles with NJ, restates Q3.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G settles with NJ, restates Q3.

text.p: Public Service Electric and Gas Co said Wednesday it has reached a settlement on three regulatory issues, including the "used and usefulness" of the Salem Nuclear Generating Station.

The Public Service Enterprise Group Inc subsidiary said it will restate third quarter earnings as a result of the agreement with the staff of the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities, and the state's Division of Ratepayer Advocate.
Under the settlements, which require approval of the board, PSE&G would provide electric customers with bill credits totaling $83.9 million in January and February 1997.
The utility said it would also forego recovery of another $12 million in energy costs that have been deferred.

The settlements would result in an earnings loss of $62.3 million, or $0.26 per Public Service Enterprise share. Of the total, $3.3 million, or $0.01 per share, had been previously recorded, and the remaining $59.0 million, or $0.25 per share, will be recorded in 1996's third quarter in anticipation of the board's approval, the company said.
Accordingly, Enterprise and PSE&G are required to restate third-quarter earnings announced on October 15.

As a result, Enterprise's restated earnings for the third quarter of 1996 are $156.0 million, or $0.64 per share, based on 243.1 million average shares outstanding, compared to $186.8 million, or $0.76 per share, based on 244.7 million average shares outstanding, in 1995's September quarter.
PSE&G's restated earnings for the third quarter are $117.8 million, or $0.48 per share, compared to $176.2 million, or $0.72 per share for the third quarter of 1995.
In addition to the regulatory settlement, PSE&G agreed with the Ratepayer Advocate to create a $30 million economic development fund and support customer assistance programs.
Under the first of the three agreements, Salem 1 and 2 nuclear units would continue in base rates without being subject to further refund, the company said.

In addition, PSE&G said, it would assume all nuclear and fossil generating fuel and performance risks, including replacement power costs associated with the nuclear stations from January 1, 1996, through December 31, 1998, the proposed expiration date of this settlement.
As a result of PSE&G's assumption of these risks, New Jersey's nuclear performance standard would not apply during the three year period, the utility pointed out.

Also, it said, the energy component of PSE&G's levelized energy adjustment charge would be fixed at its existing level, assuring PSE&G's customers of no increase in this rate until at least January 1999.
The company said the key elements of the stipulation resolving the "used and useful" issue are as follows:
-- PSE&G would provide bill credits to electric customers of $77.5 million during January and February, 1997.
-- The fixing of the energy component of PSE&G's energy charge results in the utility treating any changes in the component as revenue and expense in 1997 and 1998.

In addition, for the two years, PSE&G would have the opportunity to reduce its deferred energy cost balance. Any underrecovered or overrecovered balance that exists on December 31, 1998, would be to PSE&G's account and would not be considered in any future review of these costs.

-- Because the bill credits "fully protect ratepayers from the economic consequences of the current outages," there would be no further regulatory action regarding the "used and useful" issue through December 31, 1998.
-- If PSE&G buys out or buys down any cogeneration contracts during the stipulation period, it would be permitted to defer the costs for reviewe in a future proceeding.

-- PSE&G, the board staff and the Ratepayer Advocate reserve the right to review, in the next base rate proceeding, Salem-related capitalized costs incurred since base rates were last reviewed in 1992.
-- A new levelized energy adjustment charge rate would be established after the settlement period, with PSE&G making a filing no later than November 1, 1998.
In addition to the resolution of the Salem "used and useful" issue, the utility said, two other agreements would address separate longstanding issues it had been litigating before regulators:

-- The recovery of certain replacement power costs associated with a 58-day outage at Salem 1 in 1994 after excessive grass from the Delaware River clogged the unit's intake system. Under the proposed agreement, PSE&G would reduce its underrecovered energy cost balance by $7 million.

-- The recovery of capacity costs associated with electric utility power purchases from cogeneration producers through December 31, 1998. Under the proposal, PSE&G would provide bill credits to electric customers of $6.4 million during January and February, 1997. In addition, it would reduce its underrecovered energy costs balance by $5 million.
PSE&G said its agreement with the Rate payer Advocate, which runs through 1999, calls for PSE&G to:
-- Create a revolving economic development fund with emphasis on urban areas.
-- Provide incentives to encourage local public housing authorities to replace up to 4,000 refrigerators a year.
